frames.label: sdlc-as-questions
frames.vtt_anchor: 2:24-2:45 "Testing answers the question, does it work? But review answers the question, is what we built what we asked for?"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The whole lesson's conceptual scaffold in one slide: all five SDLC steps with their questions - Plan/What are we building?, Build/Did we make it real?, Test/Does it work?, Review/Is what we built what we asked for? (Prove it), Document/How does it work?. The '(Prove it)' suffix on Review is the lesson's thesis in two words.

frames.label: composed-workflow-script
frames.vtt_anchor: 13:12 "We have plan running in a UV single file script, build and review. It's really important that these are standalone scripts... the ADW ID is the thing that chains together the state of all of their work" (file shown again while firing off the run at 16:47)
frames.why_for_weak_student: adw_plan_build_review.py's own docstring teaches composition better than any diagram: 'This script runs: 1. adw_plan.py - Planning phase 2. adw_build.py - Implementation phase 3. adw_review.py - Review phase... The scripts are chained together via persistent state (adw_state.json).' Standalone one-purpose scripts, composed by a dumb orchestrator.

frames.label: review-screenshot-misplaced-export
frames.vtt_anchor: 31:41-31:55 "we have images uploaded... we have that down arrow... it looks like it is off here. So our agent did not obey this properly."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The review's uploaded proof (public R2 URL rendered via GitHub's camo proxy) showing the bug the review evidence exposes: the Export button floating in the middle of the Query Results header instead of directly left of Hide - exactly what the issue specified. Agent-produced screenshots let a human catch in seconds what the review agent itself missed.
frames.verified_visual: camo.githubusercontent.com image: Query Results with 'Export' mid-header (green circle) and 'Hide' far right; GitHub issue tab visible

frames.label: playwright-mcp-vision-gap
frames.vtt_anchor: 35:19-35:40 "our agent is operating Playwright... we don't have this dash dash vision. We're not operating in vision mode. The tokens aren't flowing through the vision capabilities of our language model."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The root-cause frame for why the review missed the misplaced button: .mcp.json with '--vision' typed in as a considered (and then rejected) fix. Course-era review agents took screenshots they never looked at - the single most important 'improve your review step' insight in the lesson.
